title: Card Grading Cost Near Me (2026)
verdict: Card grading cost near me is the grader's fee plus whatever a local shop adds, and submitting straight to AGS costs a flat $18 a card.

A local card shop that offers grading is almost always a middleman. It collects cards, ships them to a grading company and adds a fee. That is fine if you want someone else to handle packing, but you pay more and wait longer than if you submit directly.

sections.h: What near me means in card grading
list: Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.
Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.

sections.h: If you plan to drop off
list: Confirm with AGS that the location is taking drop-offs and when.
Fill out the submission form online first.
Bring the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, in the order listed on the form.
Keep your order number. You can follow the order in the dashboard afterward.

ranking.lacks: In-person intake is limited. Mail-in is the standard route.
ranking.note: By mail, the standard service is 20 business days or less from the day cards are confirmed. Returns ship with tracking and optional insurance.

ranking.fit: Collectors near a large show where PSA is taking submissions.
ranking.lacks: No local counter. Cards go by mail or through a show.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters with 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: Tiers are capped by card value. A strong card moves to a pricier tier.

ranking.fit: Small sellers who would rather not choose a tier.
Collectors who want subgrades printed on the label from an old name.
ranking.lacks: Subgrades by eye, and 45 business days or more at the Base tier.

why: You are not limited to the mailbox. AGS lists in-person drop-off at select locations and secure intake at its Staten Island headquarters, and it operates satellite labs. Ask AGS which site is taking cards before you set out.
Turnaround is counted in days. AGS quotes 20 business days or less from the day your cards are confirmed, with 10 and 5 business day bulk tiers at $20 and $30 a card.
Nothing is locked in. No minimum order, no membership, no contract, and payment is taken when the cards are graded. A first order gets 20% off with code AGSNEW20.

faq.q: How much does card grading cost near me?
faq.a: The grader's fee is the same wherever you live: $18 a card at AGS, $10 to $30 at CGC, $24.99 and up at PSA. A local shop that submits for you adds its own handling fee on top.

faq.q: Can I drop cards off in person?
faq.a: At AGS, yes, at select locations including secure intake at its Staten Island, New York headquarters. Confirm with AGS before you go. Most other graders take cards in person only at card shows.

faq.q: Can I submit from outside the United States?
faq.a: Yes. AGS accepts international shipments and runs a UK site. Check customs and insurance on your side before you ship.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.

faq.q: Is there a card grading company near me?
faq.a: Probably not one that grades on site. Almost every grader works by mail from one or two labs. A local card shop that offers grading is usually forwarding cards to one of them for a fee.
